title: Reported questions and commands
titleVi: Câu tường thuật: câu hỏi và câu mệnh lệnh
summary: Bỏ đảo ngữ khi kể lại câu hỏi, dùng if/whether và told/asked somebody to do — ba lỗi band 6.5 hay gặp nhất.
whyItMatters: Câu hỏi gián tiếp xuất hiện dày đặc trong Writing Task 2 (*It is unclear whether...*) và Speaking Part 3 (*I wonder why...*). Giữ nguyên trật tự câu hỏi khi đã nhúng vào câu dài là lỗi ngữ pháp rất dễ thấy, và nó kéo điểm Grammatical Range xuống ngay cả khi ý của bạn tốt.

sections.heading: Reported questions lose their inversion
body: A direct question inverts subject and auxiliary: *Where are you going?* When the question becomes part of a longer sentence, the order returns to **subject + verb**: *The officer asked us where we were going.* No inversion, no question mark.

The same rule applies to embedded questions in your own writing: *Do you know where Tom has gone?*, *I don't know who those people are*, *Can you tell me where I can find Louise?* The main clause carries the question; the embedded clause behaves like a statement.
Do-support disappears. *What time does the film start?* becomes *Do you know what time the film starts?* — the *-s* moves onto the verb and *does* is deleted.

rows: He asked us where we were going.
What time do the shops close?
She wanted to know what time the shops closed.
I wonder why she left early.
How long have you been working here?
She asked how long I had been working there.
I don't know who those people are.

sections.heading: Yes/no questions take if or whether
body: When there is no question word, English supplies one: **if** or **whether**. *Are you willing to travel?* becomes *She asked if I was willing to travel* or *She asked whether I was willing to travel.*

**whether** is the safer choice in formal writing, especially before *or not*: *It is unclear whether the policy will succeed or not.* **if** is more conversational and cannot follow a preposition: *It depends on whether prices fall* (not *on if*).
Do not use both connectors. *She asked me that if I was married* mixes two patterns; pick either *that* (statement) or *if/whether* (question), never both.

examples.right: The interviewer asked whether I had a driving licence.
I don't know if anybody saw me.
It is not clear whether the two trends are connected.
examples.wrong: It is not clear that whether the two trends are connected.

sections.heading: Commands, requests and advice
body: Reported commands use **tell/ask somebody to do something**: *The doctor told me to drink plenty of water.* The negative is **not to do**: *I told Joe not to work so hard.* The negative word goes before *to*, never after it.

The reporting verb carries the tone. **tell** is neutral or direct, **ask** is a request, **advise** is a recommendation, **warn** adds danger, **remind** implies a duty, **beg** is desperate. Choosing the right one is a vocabulary mark as much as a grammar one.

The object is obligatory: *She asked me to help her* (not *asked to help her* when the person matters). The passive version is common in formal writing: *Staff were asked to complete the form by Friday.*

rows: The doctor told me to drink plenty of water.
Jackie asked me to help her.
I told Joe not to work so hard.
My tutor advised me to apply early.
He warned me not to touch the switch.

sections.heading: Beyond say and ask: reporting verbs that carry meaning
body: A good band-7.5 answer varies the reporting verb. **admit** and **deny** report confessions; **offer**, **refuse** and **promise** report intentions; **complain**, **explain** and **insist** report stance; **suggest** and **recommend** report proposals.

Each has its own pattern. *Suggest* never takes an object plus infinitive: *She suggested that I take a taxi* or *She suggested taking a taxi* — never *suggested me to take*. *Refuse*, *offer* and *promise* take the to-infinitive with no object: *He refused to answer.*
**Explain** and **admit** can take a that-clause or a noun: *He explained that the train had been cancelled.* They do not take the *somebody to do* pattern.

examples.right: She suggested that we postpone the meeting.
examples.wrong: She suggested us to postpone the meeting.
examples.note: *Suggest* takes a that-clause or -ing, never object + to.
**admit + -ing** is the compact form; *admitted to making* is also heard.

examples.right: They refused to comment on the allegations.

sections.heading: Indirect questions as a politeness strategy
body: In Speaking Part 3, direct questions can sound abrupt. Indirect forms buy you thinking time and sound more advanced: *Could you tell me what the main causes are?* / *I wonder whether the government has considered...*

In Writing Task 2, the same structure produces excellent thesis frames: *It remains unclear whether...*, *The question is not whether X works but how it can be funded.* These are statements in disguise, so they keep statement order.
Beware the double question mark and the stray auxiliary. *I wonder what is the reason?* has two errors: the inversion after *wonder* and the question mark at the end of an embedded clause.

examples.right: I wonder why the figures were revised.
examples.wrong: I wonder why were the figures revised?
examples.note: Embedded clause: no inversion, no question mark.

examples.right: Could you tell me how much the course costs?
examples.wrong: Could you tell me how much does the course cost?
examples.note: Delete do-support in the embedded clause.

examples.right: It is unclear whether these measures will reduce emissions.
examples.note: A formal indirect question used as a thesis statement.

commonMistakes.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
commonMistakes.right: He asked me where I lived.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt giữ nguyên trật tự câu hỏi khi kể lại (*hỏi tôi sống ở đâu*), nên người học giữ luôn *did*. Câu hỏi gián tiếp dùng trật tự **chủ ngữ + động từ** và bỏ trợ động từ.

commonMistakes.wrong: She asked me that if I was married.
commonMistakes.right: She asked me if I was married.
commonMistakes.why: Không dùng đồng thời *that* và *if/whether*. Đây là lỗi lai giữa câu kể và câu hỏi, thường do dịch *hỏi rằng liệu*.

commonMistakes.wrong: He told me to not go out alone.
commonMistakes.right: He told me not to go out alone.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt đặt *đừng* trước động từ (*nói tôi đừng đi*), còn tiếng Anh đặt **not trước to**: *not to go*.

commonMistakes.wrong: She suggested me to take a taxi.
commonMistakes.right: She suggested that I take a taxi. / She suggested taking a taxi.
commonMistakes.why: *Suggest* không đi với **tân ngữ + to V**. Đây là lỗi rất phổ biến vì *advise* và *tell* lại dùng đúng cấu trúc đó.

commonMistakes.wrong: He asked me what time does the film start.
commonMistakes.right: He asked me what time the film started.
commonMistakes.why: Hai lỗi cùng lúc: giữ *does* và không lùi thì. Câu gián tiếp vừa bỏ trợ động từ vừa lùi thì theo động từ tường thuật.

ieltsTips: Mở đoạn thân bài Task 2 bằng câu hỏi gián tiếp để tạo khung lập luận: `It remains unclear whether these policies actually reduce inequality.`
Trong Speaking Part 3, dùng `I wonder whether...` hoặc `Could you tell me...` để có thêm thời gian suy nghĩ mà vẫn nghe tự nhiên.
Đa dạng động từ tường thuật: `admit`, `deny`, `claim`, `insist`, `warn` — mỗi động từ mang sắc thái riêng và được tính vào Lexical Resource.
Tuyệt đối không đặt dấu hỏi cuối câu gián tiếp; lỗi này làm câu trông như câu hỏi trực tiếp bị viết sai.

exercises.question: The interviewer asked me ___ I had ever worked abroad.
exercises.explanation: Câu hỏi yes/no không có từ để hỏi nên cần **if** (hoặc *whether*).

exercises.question: She wanted to know what time the library ___.
exercises.explanation: Động từ tường thuật *wanted* ở quá khứ nên lùi thì: **closed**. Đồng thời không dùng *does/did*.

exercises.question: The teacher told us ___ late for the exam.
exercises.explanation: Phủ định của mệnh lệnh gián tiếp là **not to + V**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He asked me where was the station.
He asked me where the station was.
He asked me where did the station was.
He asked me that where the station was.
exercises.explanation: Câu hỏi gián tiếp: trật tự **chủ ngữ + động từ**, không đảo ngữ, không *that*.

exercises.question: My manager suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.
exercises.explanation: **suggest + -ing** (hoặc *suggest that we postpone*), không dùng *suggest somebody to do*.

exercises.question: The police officer asked us where we ___ (go).
exercises.hint: past continuous after a past reporting verb
exercises.explanation: Câu trực tiếp *Where are you going?* lùi thành **were going**.

exercises.question: I'm not sure ___ the train will arrive on time or not.
exercises.explanation: Không có từ để hỏi nên cần **whether** (chuẩn hơn khi có *or not*) hoặc **if** trong văn nói.

exercises.question: The doctor advised him ___ (take) more exercise.
She warned the children ___ (not / swim) near the rocks.
Could you tell me how much this course ___ (cost)?
exercises.explanation: Câu gián tiếp giữ trật tự thường và không dùng *does*: **how much this course costs**.
